page: Microsoft Azure D2ds_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The instance features two dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core with simultaneous multithreading, running on an Intel Xeon 8370C processor clocked at 2.8 GHz. The x86_64 CPU configuration includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache, with hardware instruction set support for AVX, AVX-512 (including VNNI), AES-NI, and SHA extensions. It is provisioned with 8.0 GB of RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, and includes an 81 GB local SSD for temporary storage without bundled GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate stable single-core execution alongside predictable multi-core limitations inherent to a two-vCPU footprint. In single-threaded assessments, the instance achieves average-tier performance, marked by a Geekbench single-core score of 1586.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1873.77. Single-threaded data handling tests also reflect median performance, producing 27.36 GB/sec in gzip compression and 10.29 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. However, aggregate parallel throughput ranks in the lower percentiles across synthetic suites, yielding a Geekbench multi-core score of 1840.0, a PassMark CPU score of 2919.71, and 1.94 million operations per second in Redis SET operations.

Memory bandwidth measurements register at 102.09 GB/sec for small cached blocks, tapering to 14.24 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 13.31 GB/sec for writes. In application benchmarks, static web serving reaches 4.34 GB/sec, while lightweight LLM prompt processing on a 135M parameter model achieves 177.9 tokens per second. Given its resource density, the instance offers cost-efficient baseline hosting for non-intensive microservices, low-traffic web applications, staging environments, and basic automation workers where dedicated compute threads and local temporary SSD storage are necessary without overprovisioning hardware capacity.
description: Microsoft Azure D2ds_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by a 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon 8370C processor on the x86_64 architecture. Configured with two dedicated vCPUs on one physical core, 8.0 GB of memory, and an 81 GB local SSD, the instance delivers a standard 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio without bundled accelerators. Benchmark results show average single-core capability, reaching a 1586.0 Geekbench single-core score and 27.36 GB/sec gzip compression throughput. Multi-core performance is limited by its dual-thread scale, evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 1840.0 and a PassMark CPU mark of 2919.71. Large-block memory transfers record 14.24 GB/sec read and 13.31 GB/sec write bandwidth, while static web serving achieves 4.34 GB/sec. The instance provides an efficient baseline for lightweight web serving, microservices, staging workloads, and local cache-assisted development tasks.
